senses.example: I practice my spelling words for ten minutes after school.

senses.definition: To say that you admire or approve of someone or something.
senses.example: We praised our teammate for helping the new player.

senses.definition: Words or actions that show that you approve of someone’s work or behavior.
senses.example: The class received praise for cleaning up the yard.

senses.definition: Of great value, whether because it costs a lot or matters a lot to someone.
senses.example: The little note from Grandma is precious to me.

senses.definition: To like or want one thing more than another.
senses.example: I prefer to play outside when the sun is shining.

senses.definition: To make something ready for use or get ready to do something.
senses.example: We prepared the art table with paper, water, and brushes.

senses.definition: A gift someone gives to another person.
senses.example: Sofia wrapped a small present for her cousin.

senses.definition: Here or taking part now.
senses.example: All the players were present when practice began.

senses.definition: Happening or existing now.
senses.example: The present schedule has two more games on it.

senses.definition: To give, show, or explain something to other people.
senses.example: I will present my poster to the class tomorrow.

senses.definition: To act as if something is true for fun or to make someone believe it.

senses.definition: The amount you must pay to buy something.
senses.example: The price of each postcard was one dollar.

senses.definition: To decide how much someone must pay for something.
senses.example: We priced each cookie at fifty cents for the sale.

senses.definition: Something difficult that needs to be fixed, answered, or worked out.
senses.example: The broken latch was a problem because the gate would not stay shut.

senses.definition: A question that gives you information to work with and asks you to find an answer.
senses.example: The last math problem asked how many tiles would cover the floor.

senses.definition: Words that say what you will certainly do or what will happen.
senses.example: Jules kept her promise to return the book on Friday.

senses.definition: To say that you are sure you will do something or that it will happen.
senses.example: I promised to save my sister a seat.

senses.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
senses.example: The case protects my glasses when I put them in my bag.

senses.definition: Pleased because you or someone you care about did something well.
senses.example: I was proud of my friend when she finished the steep climb.

senses.definition: To make writing, pictures, or other work available for people to read or see.
senses.example: Our class plans to publish a book of poems.

senses.definition: To move something toward you or in the direction you are moving.

senses.definition: A steady or sudden force that draws something closer.
senses.example: One pull on the curtain cord opened the curtains.

senses.definition: Arriving or happening at the time that was planned.
senses.example: Lena was punctual and got to the bus stop before we left.

senses.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.

senses.definition: To make a hole by poking or piercing something.
senses.example: A sharp thorn punctured the soft rubber.

senses.definition: To use force to move something away from you or in a certain direction.
senses.example: We pushed the cart toward the old gate.

senses.definition: A movement or force that presses something in a direction.
senses.example: One strong push sent the empty sled down the hill.

senses.definition: To move or place someone or something somewhere.
senses.example: I put the dirty cup beside the sink.

senses.definition: To express an idea in a certain way.
